claims.claim: A Python module is a file containing Python definitions and statements, and its file name is the module name with the .py suffix removed.
An import statement searches for a named module and, after loading it, creates a binding for the module name in the importing scope.
The module search path is initialized from the script directory or current directory, PYTHONPATH, and installation-dependent defaults; sys.path exposes it.
import name keeps the module namespace available through qualified access, while from name import item binds the imported item directly in the importing scope.
Within a module, __name__ is set to the module's name when imported and to __main__ when the file is run as the top-level script.
A module is normally initialized only the first time its name is imported in a Python session, with the resulting module object retained in sys.modules.
